message.content:
Civil law—also known as **civil jurisdiction** or **private law**—regulates relationships between private parties (individuals, businesses, organizations) rather than criminal conduct. Its primary purpose is to resolve disputes, protect rights, and enforce obligations through non‑criminal means. Below are its core components: | Component | What It Covers | Key Features | |-----------|-----------------|--------------| | **Sources of Law** | • Statutory laws enacted by legislatures
• Judicial decisions (case law)
• Administrative regulations
• International treaties & conventions | • Hierarchy: Constitution > statutes > regulations
• Case law provides precedent and interpretation | | **Contract Law** | Governs agreements made voluntarily between parties | • Formation (offer, acceptance, consideration)
• Performance, breach, remedies (damages, specific performance) | | **Tort Law** | Addresses wrongful acts causing harm or loss | • Negligence, intentional wrongdoing, strict liability
• Remedies include compensatory damages, punitive damages | | **Property Law** | Regulates ownership, possession, transfer, and use of real and personal property | • Title deeds, leases, mortgages, easements | | **Family Law** | Deals with domestic relations among families | • Marriage, divorce, child custody, alimony, adoption | | **Succession / Estate Planning** | Manages distribution of assets after death | • Wills, intestate succession, probate procedures | | **Commercial/Business Law** | Focuses on business transactions and corporate governance | • Company formation, contracts, securities regulation | | **Consumer Protection** | Protects buyers from unfair trade practices | • Product safety standards, advertising truthfulness | | **Equity & Jurisprudential Principles** | Provides equitable relief when common law fails | • Injunctions, rescission, constructive trusts | ### How These Components Interact 1. **Statute → Interpretation → Application** - A statute may define contractual terms; courts interpret ambiguous clauses using established precedents. 2. **Case Law → Precedent → Predictability** - Past judgments guide future rulings, ensuring consistency across similar cases. 3. **Remedies → Enforcement Mechanisms** - Courts can award monetary compensation, order injunctions, or mandate restitution depending on the nature of the dispute. --- #### Quick Reference Checklist - [ ] Identify relevant statutory provisions - [ ] Examine prior judicial opinions for guidance - [ ] Determine whether the issue falls under contract, tort, property, family, estate, commercial, consumer protection, or another area - [ ] Evaluate available remedies (damages, injunctive relief, declaratory judgment) Understanding these building blocks helps you navigate civil litigation effectively, whether you're drafting a contract, filing a lawsuit, or seeking mediation.
message.reasoning:
The user asks: "What are the components of Civil Law?" They want an explanation. There's no tool needed; just answer with knowledge.

We should provide a concise but thorough overview of civil law's main components: sources (statutes, case law), principles (e.g., contract law, torts, property law, family law, succession). Also mention legal doctrines like equity and jurisprudence. Provide examples. No need to call any function.
